correctness.rationale: For each fixed z the recombination semantics x⊥_z y is equivalent to the fiber being empty or precisely A×B for its row/column projections. These rectangles are disjoint events under independent Bernoulli cell inclusion and give exact Q_{r,s}(p); the k fibers are independent, giving Q^k. In the sparse regime p=O(n^-5/2), two edges in different rows and columns dominate fiber failures: d_n=2 C(n,2)^2 p²(1-p)^(n²−2)+O(n^-3/2), hence n d_n→a²/2; the failure count is Bin(n,d_n)→Pois(a²/2). In the dense regime, successful nonfull rectangles require an empty row or column, probability ≤2n²(1-p)^n globally, so probability of all-full fibers p^(n³) gives e^-b, with analogous Poisson failure count. For intermediate α,β→∞: p≥1/2 yields exp(-β)+o(1); p≤1/2 and λ=n²p≤1 has ≥c λ² per-fiber failure from nonmeeting edge pairs; for λ≥1 opposite diagonal blocks independently contain edges with positive probability and their cross cells have ≥3/4 missing probability. Thus zero-success asymptotic is proved without extrapolating finite checks. Independent rectangularity enumeration checked n=2,3 and relevant finite coefficients.
